questions.question: Which naming convention is recommended for HTML class attributes in professional web engineering?
options: Semantic / functional classes based on purpose (.badge-success)
questions.explanation: Functional/semantic naming (e.g., .badge-success) keeps code maintainable when designs change.

questions.question: Why is extensive use of inline style attributes (style="...") considered an anti-pattern?
options: It violates separation of concerns, inflates HTML size, and cannot be cached effectively by browsers
Browsers refuse to render pages with inline styles
questions.hint: Separation of concerns and stylesheet caching.
questions.explanation: Inline styles bloat the markup, hinder code reuse, prevent CSS caching, and make maintenance difficult.

questions.question: What is the standard modern formatting convention for HTML tag and attribute names?
questions.explanation: The HTML standard and modern style guides strictly recommend lowercase for all tag and attribute names.

questions.question: What does the 'Separation of Concerns' principle advocate for in web architecture?
options: Keeping HTML (structure), CSS (presentation), and JavaScript (behavior) decoupled
Merging all CSS and JavaScript directly into HTML tags
Using three separate browsers for development
questions.explanation: Separation of concerns cleanly isolates structure (HTML), presentation (CSS), and logic (JS) into distinct layers.

questions.question: Which tool automatically enforces consistent formatting, quotes, and indentation across an HTML codebase?
questions.explanation: Code formatters like Prettier automatically standardize indentation, quotes, and spacing across the codebase.
